observations: What I read: AGENTS.md (in the context I was given), docs/REVISION-AND-REVIEWS.md, docs/PROMPTS.md, the whole prepared request JSON (base.script, dialoguePolicy, dialogueInstructions, files, entries, fingerprint 3d8eb9b2...), works/auto-6294ee8a2094/source/original.txt (48 lines, read in full) and works/auto-6294ee8a2094/workflow/source-coverage.json (26 spans, read in full). Every file was readable. I did not edit any file.

Reading order: I read the script in full first, inside the request JSON. I opened the original and the coverage file in the next step. Before comparing, I went back over only the dialogue and captions in panel order and judged each line without filling in context from the source.

Limitation: no artwork, storyboard or lettering exists for this stage, and I looked at no images. Nothing here certifies how panels look, where text goes or the reading order on the page. Points marked 'artwork-dependent' need checking at the storyboard, artwork and lettering stages.

Script-only reading: every line works on its own. In 01-3, 'the rest' contrasts with 'patients' and points back to the paperwork Meera lists in 01-2. In 02-2, 'here' points to the laptop setup and the WELBUK PRACTICE label in 02-1. In 02-3, Meera's opening 'And' continues Ananya's 02-2 line directly; no speech in between was removed. In 03-2, 'Of course' answers Ravi's 03-1 request. Meera knows Ravi's name in 03-4 because she registered him in 03-3. Ravi's 04-2 line answers Ananya's 04-1 question, and 'your concerns' in 04-4 refers back to it. Ravi's 05-2 question follows from Meera's 05-1 line, and 'That's the idea' in 05-3 answers it. 06-1 says 'Tomorrow ... may', so it reads as possible, not current.

Comparison with the source: all 26 dialogue and caption strings are the original wording, verbatim. No question has lost its answer, and no lines from different speakers have been merged. The only merged speech in the source is Meera's single 01-2 line, and the script splits it into two balloons by the same speaker at the ellipsis. The word order is unchanged and nothing is dropped. I accept the split: the list and the wish read as two breaths. Lettering must keep the two balloons in sequence and both tails pointing to Meera.

Each character's voice matches the source. Ananya is calm and leads ('Let's...', 'One team.', 'We'll ... together'). Meera is friendly, capable and polite ('Of course. May I...', 'That's the idea.'). Ravi is warm and plain-spoken ('Good morning!', 'Yes, please.').

Cause and effect hold: the paperwork pressure (01-2) leads to Ananya's decision (01-3), then onboarding (page 2), then smooth registration with consent (page 3), an unhurried human consultation (page 4), staying connected after the visit (page 5), and finally the vision (page 6). The comic never shows how Welbuk was chosen, but the source is a short onboarding comic and leaves this out too, so I accept the gap.

The three product roles are distinct and correctly assigned. Practice is for the clinic (02-1 label, Ananya on the laptop). Care is for staff (02-3 label, Meera's line about staff roles). Health is for patients (05-1 line, 05-2 label). 06-4 lists all three. I accept the label captions on 02-1, 02-3 and 05-2 as manga additions: the source names the product shown in each of those panels, and the labels teach readers the roles before 06-4. Each label is short and does not crowd out the art.

The future vision is kept separate from current features. 06-1 is conditional ('may'). 06-2 and 06-3 are drawn in a pale-blue vignette with a lighter palette. 06-2 has the source's 'WELBUK VISION' label plus 'The vision:'. I accept the second 'WELBUK VISION' label on 06-3: the family-wellness ecosystem is also not a launched feature, and the source asks that the vision not be shown as launched. Without that label, 06-3 could be read as a real feature of Welbuk Health. In 06-4 the vignette ends and the two closing captions (product labels and slogan) make no feature claim.

No diagnosis or medical claims: 'feeling tired lately' is a routine concern, and 04-4 talks about next steps with no treatment. The script bans prescriptions and instruments in 04-4 and text-bearing charts in the consultation room. No real patient data: every screen is abstract, the 03-3 monitor shows only blank fields, and 'Ravi' is fictional. No invented live features: 05-3 keeps 'what is available to you', and 05-2 is described as a conceptual screen.

I accept the invented appearances of the specialist, partner and child. The source requires all three in 06-2 and 06-3 but describes none of them. Every visual detail is recorded as a manga supplement in cast.settingBasis. They appear only inside the vision vignette, so they cannot be confused with the present-day cast.

Scene and time transitions, judged from the script only. 01-3 to 02-1 works: the source caption 'The clinic begins its Welbuk onboarding' covers the change; the evening setting is a supplement. 02-4 to 03-1 has no caption, as in the source. The later morning has to come from the art (morning light, the now-tidy desk with a monitor, a new character) and is artwork-dependent but acceptable. 03-4 to 04-1 works: the room changes, costumes stay the same, and 'Hello, Ravi' anchors it. 04-4 to 05-1 has no caption; the reception desk has to be recognisable again (artwork-dependent), and Meera bringing up the app as Ravi leaves is motivated enough. 05-4 to 06-1 works: 'Tomorrow' plus the train window bridges it. 06-3 to 06-4 relies on the vignette disappearing and the familiar clinic front (artwork-dependent; the transition field records this).

Ravi's 05-2 inference ('So I can keep useful information in one place?') goes beyond Meera's 05-1 words ('stay connected with their care'). It works only because he is looking at the app screen, which is also how the source sets it up. This is artwork-dependent: the 05-2 screen must visibly suggest appointment and health-information cards, or the 'So...' will read as a jump.
The only blocking item is a prop continuity contradiction in the production fields, recorded under issues below. It does not affect the dialogue.

issues.problem: The phone is never returned or put away, and the production fields contradict each other. 05-1 says patient-phone goes from Meera's hand to 'handed to Ravi'. 05-2 has Ravi holding patient-phone with 'after: held by Ravi'. 05-3 lists no props. 05-4 then gives Ravi a different 'ravi-phone' with 'before: in his pocket', and patient-phone's final state is never resolved. Readers and the image generator cannot tell whether the 05-2 phone is a clinic demo phone or Ravi's own. The next panel (05-4) contradicts 05-2's 'after'. This matters for 05-2's 'So I can keep...', which reads more naturally if it is his own phone. Fix: either make the 05-1 and 05-2 phone Ravi's own (Meera helps him on it; 05-4 and 06-1 continue with the same phone), or record the return to Meera in 05-2 'after' and 05-3 props so that 05-4 'before' is consistent. Then re-run production-audit and request a new script review.

panels.observation: Caption 'A busy day at Dr. Ananya's clinic.' matches source Page 1 Panel 1 verbatim. It is the opening line and depends on nothing earlier; it introduces Ananya by name before she speaks in 01-3. The scene keeps 'Ananya welcomes patients' and the morning Tamil Nadu setting.

Source P1-2 has one Meera line, 'Appointments, patient details, follow-ups... I wish everything were easier to manage!'. The script splits it at the ellipsis into two balloons, both Meera's, in the same order and with the same words; no other speaker's turn falls between them. The list gives 'everything' its referent within the same panel. Ringing phone, register stack and queue are kept as staging. I accept the split.

Ananya's 'Our time belongs with patients. Let's make the rest simpler.' matches source P1-3 verbatim. Read from the manga alone, 'the rest' means Meera's 01-2 paperwork as opposed to patient time, and the scene sets up her watching the desk. This is the motive for page 2.

Caption 'The clinic begins its Welbuk onboarding.' matches source P2-1 verbatim and carries the jump from the morning desk to onboarding. The label caption 'WELBUK PRACTICE for the clinic' is a manga addition naming the product the source says is on the laptop ('a clean laptop view of Welbuk Practice'). I accept it as the first of the three role labels. The screen holds only generic blank fields, as the source requires ('non-sensitive setup fields'). The evening setting is recorded as a supplement.

Ananya's 'We can organise our clinic workflow here.' matches source P2-2 verbatim. 'Here' refers to the laptop setup and the Practice label in 02-1. The scene matches the source action (enters clinic info, considers team roles), and the team-roles idea sets up Meera's 02-3 line.

Meera's 'And our team can use tools suited to each staff role.' matches source P2-3 verbatim. Its opening 'And' continues Ananya's 02-2 'We can organise...' directly, with no speech removed in between, so the shared turn holds without the source. The label 'WELBUK CARE for clinic staff' is a manga addition naming the source's staff app (Welbuk Care) and fixes Care = staff. I accept it. 'Ananya handed her the phone' in production.before is an invented action, but harmless.

Ananya's 'One team. Better coordination.' matches source P2-4 verbatim and sums up 02-2 (clinic) plus 02-3 (staff). Meera nods without speaking, a supplement consistent with 'friendly two-shot'. The page ends on a confident beat. The time jump to 03-1 has no caption, as in the source, and the art must carry it.

Ravi's 'Good morning! I'd like to see the doctor.' matches source P3-1 verbatim. It is a new scene, and the greeting and request make sense on their own. The later morning and tidy desk with monitor are supplements that the art must show (artwork-dependent). Ravi's name is held back until 03-4, after registration, which is natural.

Meera's 'Of course. May I register your details for today's appointment?' matches source P3-2 verbatim. 'Of course' answers Ravi's request to see the doctor, and the question asks for consent before any data is entered, as the source requires. The scene's open-palm asking gesture supports it.

Ravi's 'Yes, please.' matches source P3-3 verbatim and directly answers Meera's 03-2 question, so the question is kept with its answer. Only essential sample details are entered: the monitor shows blank fields from the side, and no papers or ID cards are visible. This meets the source's 'no actual identifying data'.

Meera's 'You're all set, Ravi. Please have a seat.' matches source P3-4 verbatim. 'All set' follows the 03-3 data entry, and she knows his name from registration. 'Have a seat' sets up the wait and the move to the consultation room in 04-1.

Ananya's 'Hello, Ravi. Tell me what brings you in.' matches source P4-1 verbatim. The room change is carried by the art and the use of his name (same costumes, same visit). Her open question is answered in 04-2. The laptop is closed and pushed aside, which supports the page's theme.
Ravi's 'I've been feeling tired lately.' matches source P4-2 verbatim and answers the 04-1 question directly. It is a routine concern with no diagnosis; the scene adds only a candid neck-rub.

Narration 'Technology supports the workflow. The conversation stays human.' matches source P4-3 verbatim. It is a silent listening panel: Ananya leans in and nods with the laptop closed, which shows the caption's point. There are no pronouns to resolve.

Ananya's 'We'll go through your concerns and decide the right next steps together.' matches source P4-4 verbatim. 'Your concerns' refers to the tiredness in 04-2. There is no treatment advice, and the scene bans prescriptions and instruments, as the source requires.

Meera's 'Welbuk Health is designed to help patients stay connected with their care.' matches source P5-1 verbatim. The return to reception has no caption, so it is artwork-dependent. Bringing up the app as Ravi leaves is motivated enough. 'Is designed to' is careful wording, and Health = patients is set up. This is the start of the phone-handling inconsistency recorded under issues.

Ravi's 'So I can keep useful information in one place?' matches source P5-2 verbatim. 'So' draws a conclusion that depends on the conceptual screen he is holding (artwork-dependent: the cards must suggest appointments and health information). Meera answers it in 05-3. The label 'WELBUK HEALTH for patients' is a manga addition that completes the three roles; I accept it. The screen has no text and no personal data. Prop issue: production 'after: held by Ravi' contradicts 05-4.

Meera's 'That's the idea. Let's walk through what is available to you.' matches source P5-3 verbatim. It answers Ravi's 05-2 question, so the question keeps its answer. The careful 'that's the idea' and 'what is available to you' wording is kept, so no unlaunched features are implied. Props are empty here, but the 05-2 phone is never returned or put away (see issues).

Caption 'A smoother visit. A more connected experience.' matches source P5-4 verbatim and closes the visit; Ravi waving goodbye matches 'leaves, reassured'. Prop issue: a separate 'ravi-phone' comes 'from his pocket' while the 05-2 patient-phone is still recorded as held by Ravi.

Caption 'Tomorrow, care may take us beyond our hometown.' matches source P6-1 verbatim. 'Tomorrow' and 'may' carry the jump from 05-4 and frame what follows as possible, not current. The train-window transition matches the source, and nothing is claimed as a feature.

The label 'WELBUK VISION' and the caption 'The vision: trusted connections between clinics, specialists, and patients across locations.' match source P6-2 verbatim; the source explicitly asks for that label. The pale-blue vignette and lighter palette add more separation from current features. The specialist's appearance is a manga addition, since the source gives none, and is recorded as such; I accept it.

Caption 'One connected ecosystem for care and family wellness.' matches source P6-3 verbatim. The repeated 'WELBUK VISION' label is a manga addition. I accept it because the family-wellness app is also not launched, and without the label the scene could read as a current Welbuk Health feature. The partner and child are required by the source; their looks are recorded supplements. They appear inside the vignette only.

The product-label line 'Welbuk Practice • Welbuk Care • Welbuk Health' and the final caption 'Welbuk — Building a connected healthcare ecosystem.' match source P6-4 verbatim. It is the large closing panel with Ananya, Meera and Ravi, the three roles set up earlier on 02-1, 02-3 and 05-2. The return to the present relies on the vignette disappearing and the familiar clinic front (artwork-dependent). The panel makes no feature claim, and the reader-facing thank-you is not added.
